jobs.title: Cofounder
jobs.description: Location: San Francisco Bay Area Format: In-office 4 days a week with flexibility for the occasional remote days Majordomo Mission Every generation of software creates a new operational layer. Operating systems abstracted hardware. Cloud abstracted infrastructure. Observability abstracted production systems. These categories emerged because software reached a point where every company was solving the same operational problems independently. Every company building production AI will eventually solve these problems. The only question is whether they'll solve them independently or build on a common operating layer. Building with LLMs is becoming increasingly accessible. Operating them in production isn't. Teams are making daily decisions about evaluation, routing, latency, cost and reliability, often by stitching together internal tooling. The question is whether every AI company should have to build these capabilities. We think every production AI system will eventually depend on a control plane. We'd rather build it than wait for someone else to. Majordomo will offer engineering teams the confidence to deploy, evaluate and continuously improve AI applications without building the operational infrastructure themselves. Majordomo is a portfolio company of super{set}, a venture studio that conceives, funds and builds AI-native companies from formation through scale. We work alongside founders as operators, helping shape companies from day one. We're building in a category that's still taking shape. Many of the decisions that will define how production AI is operated haven't been made yet. The opportunity is to shape how production AI is operated and help define the category. The Role We believe the next generation of infrastructure companies will be built by founders who refuse to separate engineering, product and customers into different conversations. As a Cofounder, you'll help build the company as much as the product, from early customer conversations and product direction to company building. You'll spend your time moving between customers, product and engineering, turning customer insight into products developers choose to depend on. You'll help decide what we build, why it matters, and how we bring it to market. You'll collaborate with some of the industry's most experienced builders, who have spent the last two decades building and scaling enterprise infrastructure companies. Some days you'll be reviewing architecture. Other days you'll be sitting with customers trying to understand why they didn't adopt something you thought they'd love. We don't see these as different jobs. We think they're all part of building products developers trust. Our ideal candidate is technically strong enough to earn the respect of engineers, curious enough to let customer conversations change their thinking, and pragmatic enough to know that great products are built through iteration, not certainty. You'll thrive in the ambiguity of building a company from scratch, making consequential decisions across product, engineering, customers and the business long before anyone writes the playbook. Why This Role Matters The technical challenge is only part of what we're solving. The harder challenge is earning the trust of developers. Infrastructure products become successful when developers stop evaluating them and start depending on them. That trust is earned through hundreds of product decisions that rarely make release notes. An API that feels obvious. Documentation that answers the next question before it's asked. A workflow that simplifies instead of adding complexity. A customer conversation that changes the roadmap because it revealed something fundamental. The companies that define infrastructure categories don't just build better products. They change what developers come to expect. At Majordomo, you'll help define that standard. Many of the decisions that will shape this category haven't been made yet. As a Cofounder, you'll help make them, shaping the product, the company, and ultimately how production AI is built. You'll have an outsized influence on those decisions. The choices you make in the early days won't just shape Majordomo. They'll shape what developers come to expect from AI infrastructure. What You'll Own You'll help define what developers should expect from AI infrastructure: Product strategy, customer discovery and technical go-to-market alongside the founding team. AI workflows that simplify how production systems are deployed, evaluated and improved. Developer experience across APIs, documentation and day-to-day workflows. Customer learning, translating conversations with design partners into product decisions. The quality bar across the product, from architecture to interface design. Developer adoption through products engineers recommend before anyone has to sell them. One week, you may be sitting with customers trying to understand why something that made perfect sense internally feels confusing externally. The next, you'll be deep in architecture discussions. Around here, we don't see those as different jobs. What Success Looks Like In the first 6–9 months, you will have: Established a product direction that customers consistently choose over building themselves. Built a repeatable design partner motion that continuously shapes product strategy and creates early customer advocates. Helped establish Majordomo's product, technical and commercial foundation, making decisions that scale beyond the first release. Earned the trust of engineers, customers and the founding team as a product and company builder. Shipped capabilities that simplify operating production AI while earning developer trust. Created a culture where technical excellence, customer obsession and speed of learning reinforce one another. Positioned Majordomo as a company developers recommend and design partners actively champion. Established operating rhythms that keep customer learning, product decisions and company priorities tightly aligned. What You Bring Must Have You naturally gravitate toward customers, product vision and creating the first generation of design partners. Exceptional product judgment. You know the difference between software that works and software developers choose to adopt. A track record of turning ambiguous problems into products through close collaboration with customers. The ability to move naturally between architecture discussions, product decisions and customer conversations. Experience building and shipping production software that engineers rely on. Strong technical depth and architectural judgment. You don't need to be the smartest engineer in the room, but you should earn the respect of those who are. High agency, sound engineering judgment and a pragmatic approach to balancing speed, quality and business outcomes. Experience using AI-native development tools, with the judgment to know when to trust them and when not to. Strong written communication. Great infrastructure products are often explained before they're experienced. Nice to Have You've probably done one or more of these: Experience leading developer-facing products, ideally as a Founding Product Manager. Experience selling technical products to developers. Built developer tools, infrastructure products or AI-native applications. Been an early employee or founder at a startup. Worked with LLM infrastructure, evaluation or retrieval systems. Contributed to open source or earned credibility within developer communities. Written, spoken or taught technical audiences. The Opportunity Build foundational infrastructure for production AI while the category is still being defined. Partner directly with builders and operators who have repeatedly conceived, built and scaled category-defining infrastructure companies, learning from their pattern recognition while shaping Majordomo alongside them. Shape both the product and the company from day one, with the autonomy of a Cofounder and the support of a venture studio purpose-built to create AI-native companies. Help create the standard that future AI products will build upon. If you've ever found yourself looking at AI infrastructure and thinking, "This is how it should work…". Let's talk.

jobs.location: United States (Remote) — San Francisco Bay Area Preferred
jobs.description: Location: Remote or San Francisco Bay Area (Preferred) Format: Full-time The Mission Athena is building the world's first AI tutor that teaches instead of waiting to be asked. We believe every student deserves a tutor that adapts to them, not the other way around. AI will become the foundation of personalized education, giving every student access to the kind of guidance that today only a small percentage of students can afford. Today's AI helps students find answers. Athena helps students learn. Our vision is a world where every student has access to a tutor that understands how each student learns. Athena notices when they're struggling. It knows when to encourage, when to challenge, and when to explain differently. That's the future we're building. We've already launched our first product and are working closely with students across the U.S. The biggest lesson so far is simple: students don't want another chatbot or another video. They want something that understands where they are, guides them toward what's next, keeps them motivated, and makes learning genuinely enjoyable. All-in-one education wasn't designed around the student. It's a collection of disconnected tools: students bounce between YouTube, ChatGPT, practice platforms, tutoring services, and static materials, stitching together their own learning experience. The best YouTube videos still teach everyone the same way. AI chatbots wait for students to ask the right questions. The best tutors don't. Students need software that understands what they know, what they don't know, and what should happen next. Athena combines frontier AI with thoughtful product design and learning science to create a tutor that's always available, deeply personalized, and genuinely enjoyable to learn with. We are an incubated company out of super{set}, a San Francisco venture studio that conceives, funds, and builds AI-native companies from formation through scale. Athena is founded by Kize, whose educational content has reached more than 250,000 learners. The product is already in students' hands, and we're now building the platform that can scale that experience far beyond one creator. The Role We're looking for our first Founding Engineer who will define Athena as much as the founder does and help build both the product and the technical foundation at Athena. You'll spend more time debating product decisions with the founder to turn ambitious ideas into software students genuinely love using (instead of implementing tickets). You'll help define our engineering culture, shape the product roadmap, and establish what AI-native learning should look like. This role goes well beyond engineering execution. Great education products sit at the intersection of engineering, product, design, psychology, and learning science. Every engineering decision changes how someone learns. We're looking for someone who wants to build a great company, not just write code. How We Build We care as much about how we build as what we build. Product taste and good design matter. We believe great design keeps students engaged. We obsess over the moments most teams ignore: the pacing of an explanation, the moment encouragement appears, the friction between opening the app and making progress. We want Athena to feel less like educational software and more like a product students genuinely look forward to using. If Athena feels like "another AI app," we've failed. Students' outcomes win every argument. Every decision starts with one question: does this genuinely help students learn? Ship early and learn fast. We believe real student behavior is more valuable than internal debate. We ship, observe, learn, and iterate relentlessly. AI should raise the quality bar. We use AI throughout our development process to move faster, but never to lower our standards. AI should amplify craftsmanship, not replace it. Why This Role Matters The hard problem is building software students trust enough to learn with every day. That means solving personalization, memory, motivation, evaluation, and product design at once. As Athena's first Founding Engineer, you'll help define what AI-native education looks like. You'll influence not only the architecture, but also the product, the culture, and the standards we build around. The architectural decisions you make in year one may still shape Athena a decade from now. What You'll Own You'll own the following across both product and engineering: Designing learning experiences students genuinely enjoy using Helping every student make measurable progress through personalized, AI-powered tutoring Defining how Athena remembers what students know and decides what they should learn next Building the systems that measure whether students are actually learning and not just completing exercises Establishing the engineering architecture, tooling, and standards that allow Athena to move quickly as we scale Partnering with the founder on product direction, technical strategy, and building the engineering team At a skill level, you'll work across: Full-stack product development spanning frontend, backend, AI systems, and infrastructure Production AI systems that combine reasoning, retrieval, evaluation, and continuous improvement from student interactions Product quality, performance, and user experience Engineering architecture, developer tooling, and infrastructure that enable rapid, high-quality iteration This role spans the entire stack. One week you may be designing a new learning experience or refining how Athena adapts to an individual student. The next week, you may be improving AI evaluation systems, optimizing infrastructure, strengthening engineering foundations, or shipping features inspired directly by student feedback. What Success Looks Like During your first 6 to 9 months, your focus will be on three priorities. Students voluntarily return every week: Build the next versions of Athena and the learning experiences that students return to because they genuinely help them make progress. Engineering velocity increases rather than slows: Establish scalable architecture, engineering standards, and systems that allow the company to move quickly without sacrificing quality. Partner closely with the founder on product direction, architecture, hiring, and engineering culture: As one of the earliest employees, you'll help shape not only the product, but how Athena operates. What You Bring Must Have Experience building and shipping production software across multiple layers of the stack. You've built full products real customers depend on. Strong product instincts and engineering judgment. You instinctively know when something feels unfinished. Exceptional attention to user experience and product quality. You care about details most people never notice. The ability to turn ambiguous ideas into polished, intuitive products. Experience talking directly with users and incorporating feedback into product decisions. You regularly sync with users because product intuition isn't built from dashboards. A track record of operating independently in early-stage or fast-moving environments. AI makes you faster, not less rigorous, accelerating development without compromising quality. You want to spend the next several years building something from zero. We're less interested in your exact technology stack than your judgment, curiosity, and ability to build products people genuinely love. Nice to Have Experience as an early engineer or founder Experience building consumer products Experience building AI-native products Experience with LLMs, agents, retrieval systems, evaluation frameworks, or AI infrastructure Passion for education and helping people learn This role probably isn't for you if You prefer clear requirements over ambiguous problems You want someone else deciding what to build You're optimizing for elegant architecture instead of student outcomes You see engineering as separate from product What You Get A defining role as the first engineer at an AI-native education company Direct partnership with the founder on product and technical strategy Competitive salary and meaningful equity Ownership over both technical and product direction from day one The opportunity to help define the future of personalized education How to Apply Please include: Your résumé or LinkedIn profile Show us something you've built that people actually use. We'd rather explore one product deeply than skim ten GitHub repositories. A few sentences about why Athena's mission resonates with you. We're looking for someone who wants to invent how millions of students learn with AI, not to implement a roadmap. If that excites you more than the title on your business card, we'd love to meet you.
